description: Integraremos un equipo multidisciplinario de especialistas y entusiastas de la ingeniería aeronáutica, formados en las aulas y hangares del IPN. Combinamos una sólida base técnica en aerodinámica, sistemas de navegación, cálculo avanzado y programación con una visión innovadora enfocada en resolver desafíos complejos del mundo real y aeroespacial.
summary: We developed a digital tool designed to estimate lunar surface parameters and evaluate the viability of safe lunar landings. By integrating real-time NASA databases with high-resolution imagery captured by the Artemis II mission, the platform allows users to analyze critical environmental variables—including surface temperature, solar illumination, and exact selenographic coordinates (latitude and longitude). Users can assess landing viability using either historical Apollo mission sites or custom user-defined coordinates. Through real-time data processing, the tool calculates and proposes optimal landing windows, providing mission planners with actionable insights to mitigate thermal and visibility risks during descent and moonlanding.
details:
This project was created using Python 3.10. Using PyCharm as the IDE, Flask handles the local server and API, HTML, CSS and JavaScript handles the visuals. SQLite handles storing previous assessments. ReportLab creates PDF files. The CSV module in Python handles exporting the data. The program can be run locally using a web browser on localhost:8080. No specialist equipment is needed.

AI tools were used throughout the project. Gemini was used at the Argon level to help with the maths and checking operations involved in calculating the lunar environment. This made it easier to analyze and understand some of the maths processes. Cloud was used as a coding assistant to aid with writing, organizing, checking and correcting code. It also identified possible errors in the code. This helped optimize the development time.

This project has been innovative as it combines science with an interactive interface similar to a mission control centre. You can see a 3D representation of the moon with procedural texturing and fake craters. Alongside this there is telemetry data, graphs and reports that can be downloaded.

Throughout the development process the team considered how easy the program would be to use, how accessible it is, having it in modules, validating the coordinates, UTC dates/times and storing data locally. We also had limitations with our models, the moon is just a visual and does not represent realistic terrain. The temperatures and illumination data is approximate. The Earth visibility is just a geometric representation and the initial assessment is based on heuristics.

This project should be seen as an educational tool to show how software development, science and AI can be combined to aid the initial research into possible lunar landing sites.
